items.description: In the three weeks since the alleged murder of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby in Alice Springs, the NT's child protection system has come under intense scrutiny. Now, former child protection workers are speaking out about why they believe the system is broken.

items.title: Trump says US may strike Iran again within days

featured_image.name: Trump reiterates Iran nuclear talking points despite swirling questions

items.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the United States may need to attack Iran again, revealing he was just an hour away from ordering a new strike before he postponed the operation. The remarks came a day after Trump called off what he described as a "very major attack" that had been scheduled for Tuesday, at the request of Gulf allies who said diplomatic negotiations were making progress.

items.title: NATO weighs naval mission in Hormuz as strait nears four months of closure

featured_image.name: Countries to Meet on Hormuz Naval Mission Led by UK, France

items.description: NATO is actively discussing a potential naval deployment to help secure commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz if the waterway remains blocked into early July, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing a senior alliance official. The discussions mark a shift for the alliance, which earlier this year refused to participate in the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports but now faces mounting pressure as the disruption to one of the world's most critical shipping routes approaches its fourth month.[1]

items.title: Google I/O 2026 kicks off today with Gemini AI updates

featured_image.name: Google I/O 2026 starts tomorrow: How to watch and what to expect ...

items.description: Google is rolling out a slate of updates to its Gemini AI assistant just as Google I/O 2026 kicks off today, May 19, at Shoreline Amphitheatre in Mountain View, California. Among the most notable additions is a "thinking level" control that lets users choose how much reasoning the model applies to their prompts — addressing a longstanding complaint about fixed reasoning modes.

items.title: Russia claims Ukraine plans drone strikes from Latvia, threatens Riga

featured_image.name: Russia's foreign intelligence service claims Ukraine preparing drone ...

items.description:
Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) claimed on Monday that Ukraine is preparing to launch drone strikes against Russian targets from Latvian military bases, an accusation swiftly rejected by both Riga and Kyiv as disinformation.

The SVR alleged that soldiers from Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces had already been deployed to military installations in Latvia, and that Kyiv intended to use Latvian territory — not just airspace — as a launching platform for attacks, calculating that shorter flight distances would increase the effectiveness of strikes. The agency added a veiled threat, stating that "the coordinates of decision-making centers on Latvian territory are well known" and that NATO membership "will not protect those who aid terrorists from just retribution".[1][2]

items.title: Iran offers to send enriched uranium to Russia in amended US peace plan

featured_image.name: Iran ready to transfer uranium stockpiles to Russia as part of peace ...

items.description: Iran has proposed transferring its stockpile of approximately 400 kilograms of highly enriched uranium to Russia rather than the United States, according to leaked details of Tehran's amended peace proposal reported by Al Arabiya on Monday. The offer marks a shift in Iran's negotiating posture and comes as President Donald Trump paused a planned military strike to allow diplomacy to continue.[1][2]

items.title: China secretly trained 200 Russian troops now fighting in Ukraine, Reuters reports

featured_image.name: ‘Old friend’ Putin and China’s Xi strengthen strategic ties at summit

items.description: China's armed forces covertly trained approximately 200 Russian military personnel in China late last year, with some of those soldiers having since returned to fight in Ukraine, according to an exclusive report by Reuters. The revelation, published as Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, marks a new threshold in military cooperation between the two countries.[1][2]

items.title: Iran details peace proposal demanding reparations, end of blockade

featured_image.name: What's Iran's 14-point proposal to end the war? And will Trump ...

items.description:
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed on Tuesday that Tehran's latest peace proposal to the United States includes the lifting of sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian funds, and an end to the U.S. naval blockade, according to a Reuters report citing Iran's state news agency IRNA. The proposal also calls for a ceasefire on all fronts, including Lebanon, the exit of U.S. forces from areas near Iran, and reparations for destruction caused by the war.[1]

The terms appear largely unchanged from Iran's previous offer, which President Donald Trump rejected last week as "garbage".[1]

items.title: Deputy Secretary Landau helped secure visa for fugitive Polish minister

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Trump official helped secure US visa for fugitive Polish minister  | Reuters

items.description:
U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau personally directed senior officials to facilitate a visa for Zbigniew Ziobro, a fugitive former Polish justice minister facing 26 criminal charges, enabling him to flee Hungary for the United States, according to a Reuters exclusive report citing three people familiar with the matter.[1][2]

Landau instructed officials from the State Department's Consular Affairs Bureau to order the U.S. embassy in Budapest to issue the visa, describing the matter as "a national security issue," one source told Reuters. One source described the document as a journalist visa, a characterization that aligns with earlier Polish media reports suggesting Ziobro may be working as a correspondent for TV Republika, a right-wing Polish broadcaster. The sources told Reuters they were unaware of any involvement by President Donald Trump, and it remained unclear what role Secretary of State Marco Rubio played.[3][4][2][1]

items.title: Mexico, Uruguay aid ship docks in Havana amid Cuba crisis

featured_image.name: 2 Mexican Navy ships laden with humanitarian aid dock in Cuba as US  blockade sparks energy crisis

items.description: A vessel carrying humanitarian aid from the governments of Mexico and Uruguay docked in Havana on Monday, offering a measure of relief to a nation gripped by its worst energy crisis in decades. The ship, named the Asian Katra, arrived in Havana Bay loaded with food supplies and personal hygiene products as Cuba endures blackouts lasting more than 20 hours a day in parts of the capital.[1][2][3]

items.title: Jury sides with OpenAI, rejects Musk's lawsuit

featured_image.name: Jury Sides With OpenAI, Sam Altman in Case Brought by Elon Musk - WSJ

items.description: A federal jury in Oakland, California, sided with OpenAI and Sam Altman on Monday, rejecting Elon Musk's lawsuit alleging the artificial intelligence company betrayed its nonprofit mission when it shifted toward a for-profit model. The nine-member jury found that Musk's case was filed too late, ending the closely watched legal battle that had threatened to upend one of the most valuable private companies in the world.
